newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan pork export ban seen hitting corn imports.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan pork export ban seen hitting corn imports.

text.p: Taiwanese corn imports are seen falling sharply after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease that has ravaged the country's pork industry, traders said on Friday.
A Reuters survey of five major Taiwan grain importers found that all expected sharp reductions in corn imports.
"Corn imports will drop significantly," one buyer said.
The consensus among importers would be for corn imports to plunge by 1.2 million tonnes representing 19 percent of the island's annual corn imports of 6.5 million tonnes.
The ban on exports of fresh and frozen pork prompted Taiwanese buyers to call off three grains and oilseeds tenders on Friday involving up to 132,000 tonnes of corn and 64,000 tonnes of soybeans.
Japan and South Korea have already banned pork imports from Taiwan.

Taiwan Sugar Corp cancelled a tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans. The Members Feed Industry Group on Friday also passed on a tender for up to 112,000 tonnes of corn.
The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association likewise passed on a tender for a 54,000 tonne shipment of Argentine or Brazilian soybeans.
Traders said the impact on soybean imports would be limited as only a small portion of soymeal is used for animal feed.
"Soybean imports could drop a little, as soymeal demand is expected to fall," a soybean buyer said.
Traders estimated that Taiwan's soybean annual imports may declined seven to eight percent after the ban. A more accurate estimate should be available next week.
Freight cost from the U.S. Pacific Northwest was seen at about US$14.00 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico ranged between $24.50 and $25.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
